newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SOCCER-SWEDEN REKINDLE WORLD CUP HOPES WITH WIN OVER SCOTLAND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SWEDEN REKINDLE WORLD CUP HOPES WITH WIN OVER SCOTLAND.

text.p: Sweden restored their chances of qualifying for the 1998 World Cup finals on Wednesday with a comfortable 2-1 victory over a shambolic-looking Scotland.
Sweden's lanky Bologna striker Kennet Andersson was the hero of the evening, scoring each side of the interval as the home team imposed total dominance on Scotland.

Scotland, looking far from the team that heads the World Cup qualifying group four, never got into the game and had to settle for a consolation goal from Blackburn striker Kevin Gallacher from the visitors' first corner seven minutes from time.

Sweden's mercurial striker Martin Dahlin made both of Andersson's goals, nodding the ball back in the 43rd minute for Andersson to hammer an unstoppable volley past Leighton to give the Swedes a 1-0 halftime lead.

In the 63rd minute Dahlin slid the ball past a square and stranded Scottish defence for Andersson to slot home a second goal that puts Sweden's World Cup quest firmly back on track and makes Scotland's group lead look somewhat shaky.

Both Sweden and Austria have two games in hand over Scotland, who stay on 14 points, just four ahead of Austria, who beat Estonia 2-0, and five clear of Sweden. These three teams look set to battle for the two qualifying spots.
Swedish coach Tommy Svensson, under pressure for a victory after a weak World Cup campaign, was relieved at the outcome.
"It was a wonderful evening and we played some great football," he said, paying tribute to Andersson and Leicester City midfielder Pontus Kamark.
Sweden attacked from the outset, with Andersson testing Jim Leighton with two testing shots in the first five minutes.
The home side suffered a blow in the sixth minute when Stefan Schwarz was forced to leave the field after a hard challenge which left him with a fractured shin and his leg in plaster..
Sweden pressed throughout the first half, Anderlecht's Per Zetterberg coming close with a delicately flighted free kick in the 22nd minute.
Dahlin, the mercurial star of the Swedish attack, gradually played himself into the match, shaking off the physical close marking of Scotland's central defender Colin Hendry to threaten.
In the 29th minute the Scottish defence was caught napping by a low struck corner and Dahlin's gentle shot neat Leighton only to be cleared off the line by Paul Lambert.

With Sweden dominating and Scotland seemingly looking for a draw, Dahlin nodded back a deep ball into the Scottish penalty area for Andersson to rifle home a fierce volley from 20 metres to give Sweden a 1-0 half-time lead.
Sweden should have scored again when Anderlecht midfielder Per Zetterberg left Scottish keeper Jim Leighton stranded with a floated shot that hit the underside of the bar in the 55th minute.
Scotland's performance went from bad to worse in the second half. The defence resorted constantly to fouls to thwart the fast-turning Swedish attack and the attack was totally lacking in inspiration.
Gallacher's goal, slotted home as the Swedish defence slumbered briefly, induced some anxious moments for home spectators but Scotland did not look too anxious to press for the draw.
